chunks: From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever feeds a believer from hunger, Allah will feed him from the fruits of Paradise; and whoever quenches a believer from thirst, Allah will quench him from the Sealed Nectar.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for feeding a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) emphasizes the spiritual merit of satisfying a believer's physical needs, linking earthly sustenance to divine reward. It specifically promises the giver sustenance from the fruits of Paradise and the 'Sealed Nectar' (al-Rahiq al-Makhzum), a high-grade drink reserved for the righteous, thereby elevating the act of charity to a means of attaining eternal bliss.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup class="bTxt">asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who feeds a Momin from hunger, Allahazwj would Feed him from the fruits of the Paradise; and the one who quenches a Momin from thirst, Allahazwj would Quench him from the Sealed Nectar (الرَّحِيقِ الْمَخْتُومِ)’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from Hammad from Ibrahim from abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Whoever provides food to a believer to satisfy his hunger Allah will feed him with the fruits of paradise and whoever provides water to quench the thirst of a believer Allah will quench his thirst from the wine of paradise which is in sealed containers.”
